features.description: The near side of the 3-kpc arms that hug the ends of the Galactic bar, seen in front of the Galactic centre and approaching us at about 53 km/s (Dame & Thaddeus 2008). Only three maser parallaxes are assigned to it, so its fitted geometry is poorly constrained; Reid et al. regard the 3-kpc arms as a phenomenon of the bar rather than one of the four major arms. Label anchored at the kink position of Reid et al. 2019 Table 2 (R0 = 8.178 kpc used for the Sun).

features.description: The arm segment the Sun lives in, between the Sagittarius-Carina and Perseus arms; it contains the Orion Nebula and the Cygnus star-forming regions. Reid et al. 2019 consider it an isolated segment rather than one of the four major arms. Single pitch angle (no kink fitted). Label anchored at the kink position of Reid et al. 2019 Table 2.

features.description: Far-side counterpart of the expanding 3-kpc arm, discovered in CO by Dame & Thaddeus 2008 as a faint lane at positive velocities parallel to the near arm. It is not in Reid et al. 2019 Table 2 (no maser parallaxes). Dame & Thaddeus assume both 3-kpc arms have the same Galactocentric radius (3.3 kpc for R0 = 8.5 kpc) and that the far arm stays at 11.8 kpc from the Sun along its length; the drawn line follows that assumption over the longitudes they averaged (-12 to +8 deg), so its geometry is approximate. Label at l = 0, 11.8 kpc.

features.description: The Milky Way is a barred spiral. The long bar is a flat extension of the boxy/peanut bulge, traced by red clump giants out to about 5 kpc from the centre; its near end points towards positive Galactic longitude. Wegg, Gerhard & Portail 2015 find the long bar at 28-33 deg to the Sun-centre line, slightly more than the 27 +- 2 deg of the bulge region (Bland-Hawthorn & Gerhard 2016). Label at Sgr A*.

features.description: The bulge of the Milky Way is the thick inner part of the bar, buckled into a box or peanut shape with an X-shaped structure seen in red clump stars. It holds old, mostly metal-rich stars. Masses are dynamical-model values (Portail et al. 2017 include the long bar; Bland-Hawthorn & Gerhard 2016 quote the region mapped by the VVV survey). Label at Sgr A*.

features.description: The thin disc holds most of the Galaxy's stars, gas, dust and all of its young stars and spiral arms. Its density falls exponentially with radius and with height; the scale height grows outwards (see Flare). Values from the review of Bland-Hawthorn & Gerhard 2016. Label at Sgr A*.

features.description: Beyond about 8 kpc from the centre the Galaxy's disc bends like the brim of a hat: up (north) on the side of the first and second quadrants, down (south) in the third and fourth quadrants, as mapped in 3D with classical Cepheids. Model of Chen et al. 2019 (power law, all Cepheids): z_w = 0.060 (R - 7.72)^1.33 sin(phi - 17.5 deg), z_w and R in kpc, phi measured from the Sun's direction in the sense of Galactic rotation (the same sense as the spiral-arm azimuth beta). With this sense z_w is negative in the fourth quadrant, which matches the southern warp at 240 < l < 330 deg seen by Skowron et al. 2019. For R > 9 kpc Chen et al. also fit a linear law (R_w = 9.26 kpc, phi_w = 17.4 deg, a = 0.148). Skowron et al. 2019 fit a quadratic surface instead (z1 = 0.0152 per kpc, R_d = 8 kpc, line of nodes -28 deg) that reaches 0.74 kpc at R = 15 kpc. Label anchored at R = 15 kpc, phi = -72.5 deg (deepest point of the southern warp, about 15 kpc from the Sun towards l of about 284 deg), 0.84 kpc below the plane by the Chen et al. law.

features.description: The stellar disc gets thicker with distance from the centre: from about 0.25 kpc at the Sun's radius the thin disc's scale height grows threefold by 15 kpc and about eightfold by 20 kpc. Law of López-Corredoira & Molgó 2014 (SDSS-SEGUE F8V-G5V stars, best fit 'all data, no metallicity gradient'): h_z(R) = 0.24 kpc [1 - 0.037 (R - 8) + 0.052 (R - 8)^2], R in kpc; the thick disc flares as 0.71 kpc [1 + 0.021 (R - 6.9) + 0.006 (R - 6.9)^2] beyond 6.9 kpc. Uncertainties of the flare terms are large but exclude no flare. Gaia EDR3 star counts (Chrobáková et al. 2022) give a similar thin-disc flare and a stronger thick-disc flare. Label anchored in the plane at R = 15 kpc towards the Galactic anticentre.

features.description: A faint, roughly spheroidal cloud of old, metal-poor stars and globular clusters surrounding the disc, built largely from accreted dwarf galaxies; Deason et al. 2019 argue that its inner part is dominated by the debris of one massive dwarf galaxy accreted about 10 Gyr ago. Its density falls as about r^-2.5 inside the break radius and more steeply outside. Deason et al. 2019 (Gaia DR2 red giants, Kroupa mass-to-light ratio 1.5) find 1.4e9 Msun, larger than the 4-7e8 Msun quoted by Bland-Hawthorn & Gerhard 2016. Label at Sgr A*; r is the break radius.

features.description: Our galaxy, a barred spiral with a central boxy/peanut bulge, a thin and a thick stellar disc, four major spiral arms plus the Local Arm, and a faint stellar halo, all embedded in a much more massive dark-matter halo. The Sun's distance comes from the orbit of the star S2 around Sgr A* (GRAVITY Collaboration 2019, statistical error 13 pc, systematic 22 pc); its height above the mid-plane from Gaia DR2 star counts (Bennett & Bovy 2019). Label at Sgr A*.
